decisions.quote: The purpose of the present research was to replicate two experiments in which neonatal imitation was reported. In replicating the first experiment tongue- and lip-protrusion, mouth-opening, and sequential finger movement were modeled for six 2-week-old babies.
decisions.reason: Neither prior_adjudication_path nor prior_state_path exists on disk (never adjudicated). The supplied source text (592d372d41a77ec8.txt) contains only the 4-line title, authors, and abstract of Koepke, Hamm, Legerstee, & Russell (1983) ('Neonatal imitation: Two failures to replicate', 10.1016/s0163-6383(83)80012-5). The abstract states that the research replicated two experiments in which neonatal imitation was reported (the first modeling tongue- and lip-protrusion, mouth-opening, and sequential finger movement for six 2-week-old babies; the second modeling mouth-opening and tongue-protrusion for 14 babies aged 17-21 days) and that both replications failed to yield evidence of neonatal imitation. However, the abstract never names or cites the original authors, year, or paper(s). While shipped row 319 is Meltzoff & Moore (1977) ('Imitation of Facial and Manual Gestures by Human Neonates', Science, 10.1126/science.198.4312.75), which reported two experiments matching these procedures, the abstract text alone cannot verify the target identity or rule out whether both replicated experiments come solely from shipped row 319 versus an additional unshipped paper.
